exercises.q: Из Назарета ___ (мочь + ли) быть что доброе?
exercises.prompt: Nazareth! Can anything good come from there?
exercises.why: The English conjunction "if" introducing a conditional clause has the Russian equivalent ЕСЛИ. But the English "if", equivalent of "whether", expresses an indirect question or doubt and has the Russian equivalent ЛИ. The particle ЛИ never begins the clause; it takes the second place in the clause following the word to which the question or doubt refers: *Спроси его, говорит ли он по-немецки. Он спросил меня, живу ли я здесь. Я не знаю, сделают ли они это.* But: *Мы дадим ему работу, если он говорит по-немецки. Sometimes ЛИ is used in direct questions, especially in those expressing a doubt: *Был ли он там? Не опоздал ли он на поезд?* Notice also constructions: negative infinitive + ЛИ,… — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 91.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: The English conjunction "if" introducing a conditional clause has the Russian equivalent ЕСЛИ. (From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 91)
